headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-session memory and customer-support data create plausible prompt-injection, leakage, and workflow-conflict pathways, but B is non-runnable and networkless so blast radius is bounded.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a has session memory and handles documents/customer-support data, so if agent_b outputs are copied into its inputs, malicious instructions could persist. agent_b is a course artifact with no runtime surfaces, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly documented; uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF agent_b content is manually pasted into agent_a sessions
IF agent_a treats document text as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation prompt
Review pasted content for imperative language before reuse
Disable session carryover for untrusted inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported text

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches personal and finance data and can egress to allowlisted network destinations; agent_b has no network egress and no data classes, so leakage is mainly from agent_a exporting sensitive context into shared workflows or copied outputs. The pairwise path exists in default documentation, but B itself is not a data sink.
conditions: IF agent_a receives personal or finance data in the same session
IF agent_a outputs are copied into external systems or logs
mitigations: Minimize sensitive fields before sending to agent_a
Turn off verbose logging for sessions with personal data
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction on agent_a outputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a supports multiple instances with session memory, but agent_b is non-runnable and has no write or network surfaces. There is no documented shared mutable resource, so only a weak coordination risk remains if an operator manually reuses artifacts between them.
conditions: IF an operator manually shares the same workspace artifacts between both agents
IF both are run concurrently against the same files outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Use separate folders for each agent
Avoid concurrent edits to the same artifact

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can generate decisions, workflows, and expert SQL queries, which agent_b could reuse as course material or operator input. Because agent_b is not runnable and has no verification or action-taking surface, the cascade is indirect, but the pair still supports unverified reuse of A's outputs.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are treated as authoritative by an operator
IF agent_b-derived materials are reused without independent verification
mitigations: Require a human check before reusing agent_a outputs
Mark agent_a outputs as unverified drafts
Cross-check SQL or workflow steps against source systems
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream use

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while agent_b touches none and has no residency or retention fields. That makes a compliance mismatch plausible only through agent_a's handling and operator workflows, not through a documented cross-agent transfer; the other agent is cited to show the absence of a second regulated sink.
conditions: IF personal data or finance data is routed through agent_a
IF retention or residency requirements apply to copied outputs
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to agent_a
Keep a local record of data-handling decisions
Confirm allowlisted egress destinations are compliant
